look_here_first: Inspect fruit first when present: bur oak has a large nut buried deeply in a broad mossy cup with soft projecting scale tips forming a shaggy fringe. Without fruit, look for a broad fiddle-shaped leaf with VERY deep middle/proximal sinuses (a narrow waist), then much shallower distal lobes or teeth. Corky wings on some older twigs provide a supporting character.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: large leaves often broadest toward tip with deep middle sinuses creating a waist

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upper blade often shallowly lobed beyond the deep middle sinuses

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: cupule commonly encloses one-half or more of nut and bears long soft fringe around rim

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Adult leaf often 70–150 × 50–130 mm but highly variable (occasionally 310 × 160 mm), deepest sinuses near middle or basal two-thirds, sometimes almost reaching midrib; distal portion broad and less deeply lobed.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaf underside pale to whitish with dense minute appressed stellate hairs; hairs alone may overlap with other white oaks.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Twigs 2–4 mm, may bear flat radiating corky wings/ridges; buds 2–5(–6) mm, usually glabrous.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Acorns large: nut generally 25–50 mm long, cup ~15–50 mm deep × 20–60 mm wide enclosing half to seven-eighths or more of nut.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Cup scales near rim may project 5–10 mm or longer SOFT awns forming unmistakable mossy fringe (fringe reduced in some northern/western populations).

key_traits.label: Oak training
key_traits.text: Use leaf architecture plus bark/twig/buds and mature acorn/cupule; never identify an oak from leaf silhouette alone.
